title: insar-rs: A native Rust engine for InSAR time-series ground deformation (PS-InSAR + SBAS)
description: A native Rust engine for InSAR time-series analysis of ground deformation from Sentinel-1 data, covering Persistent Scatterers (PS-InSAR) and Small-Baseline Subset (SBAS). The field is dominated by Python/MATLAB stacks (ISCE, StaMPS, MintPy, EZ-InSAR); insar-rs provides a dependency-light, parallel (Rayon) native engine consumable as a library, CLI (insar), and Python bindings (insar-rs on PyPI). insar-core spans 14 modules: own in-memory stack I/O plus a native ISCE reader (VRT + raw, mmap), PS selection, small-baseline network design, quality-guided 2D phase unwrapping (with an optional SNAPHU backend), phase-closure unwrap-error correction, SBAS inversion (OLS / coherence-weighted WLS / robust L1-IRLS) with DEM-error estimation, formal velocity uncertainty and bootstrap, stratified and GACOS/ERA5 tropospheric correction, deramping, LOS-to-vertical/east decomposition, per-pixel ML features, and an end-to-end run_sbas pipeline. Raster I/O uses the sibling SurtGIS native GeoTIFF writer (no GDAL). Numerical parity with MintPy is certified on the Fernandina Sentinel-1 stack: displacement-series RMSE 0.0029 mm, velocity RMSE 0.0070 mm/yr, r = 1.000000. This deposit archives the v0.2.0 release (published to crates.io as insar-core and to PyPI as insar-rs).
